items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names describe intent (renderStatsAndLogs, openDangerModal, handleImportFromTextarea, pendingRestocks) and formatting is consistent. Single-letter names (o, r, p, v, l) appear only as loop or lambda iterators. Section comments mark each block.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One new 3833-line file, so the >500-line cap applies. UI handlers call the shopTestAPI methods, which is good layering. But renderStatsAndLogs mixes stats, the SKU table and logs, and recomputes pending restocks from state.orders in the UI. UI functions reach shared state through window.* globals.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Operations return {ok,error}, and import is validated with an error shown and no overwrite. Gaps: FileReader has no onerror handler, and stock thresholds such as 'v.stock <= 5' are hard-coded magic numbers. I could not see most of the validation code because the diff was truncated.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Has a generic dangerous-action modal (reset confirm) and cancel confirmation, toasts, status badges and a coupon rule note. But handleImportFromTextarea calls importData straight away with no confirmation before overwriting data. Refund/restock confirmation is only implied by the after-sale modal.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: UI actions and stats go through window.shopTestAPI (requestAfterSale, getStats, importData), and stats are computed each time. Prices appear to be stored as yuan floats ('v.price.toFixed(2)'), and I could not confirm integer-cent arithmetic. The UI duplicates the pending-restock count.
